_comment: Spec for build_readme_assets.py. Every {key} is substituted from summary.json, which build_summary.py derives from the CSV. A renamed fact fails the build rather than shipping a blank.

hero.name: hero
hero.title: What's On Netflix
hero.subtitle: A Power BI catalogue explorer over {source[kept_rows]:,} Netflix titles - what the library is made of, where it comes from, and when it landed. Built from one Kaggle CSV, kept as diffable PBIP text.

banners.name: section-data
banners.title: The dataset
banners.body: One Kaggle CSV, {source[raw_rows]:,} rows and {source[columns]} columns describing every title Netflix listed up to September 2021. Messier than it looks.

banners.name: section-shape
banners.title: Making it answerable
banners.body: Three columns held lists, not values. Splitting them turns a spreadsheet into something you can ask questions of.

banners.name: section-findings
banners.title: What the catalogue actually looks like
banners.body: The United States holds {findings[us_titles]:,} titles. {findings[tv_ma]:,} carry a TV-MA rating. The library stopped growing in {findings[peak_year]}.

banners.name: section-build
banners.title: How it is built
banners.body: One shared query feeds two tables, and the bridge lost {model[reduction_factor]}x its rows without changing a single number on the page.
